object_description: compact volume turned slightly away from the prevailing geometries around a two-storey hall
design_condition: the compact volume sits in the south-eastern part of the site turned slightly away from the surrounding geometries, generating differentiated outdoor spaces and leaving a generous green belt free to the north

positive: The slightly rotated position generates differentiated outdoor spaces for school and neighbourhood
It mediates between the adjacent green and compact urban bodies
A generous green belt remains free in the northern part of the site
A few individual trees structure the open meadow and form the connection to the park
The playground is associated with the school and framed by freely positioned trees
Break area and parking are bordered by tree-lined green areas creating a subtle, permeable transition
A comprehensible route connects the school and green spaces to the surroundings
The address is created from the south via the spacious playground
The two main entrances are marked by arcades and separated by an air space overlooking the pool
A two-storey hall with a skylit multi-purpose hall is surrounded by canteen, library and staff rooms
Extra heights create exciting visual links between different uses and differentiate the floors
The architectural expression is kept simple and the compact volume designed uniformly on all sides
Dominant horizontal concrete bands emphasise the horizontal structure
Set-back concrete pillars with filigree window divisions differentiate the levels
The design is impressive in terms of urban planning
negative: The all-weather area on an embankment makes the zoning between green belt and school outdoor space too dominant
The extra heights produce a large volume with a negative impact on construction costs and sustainability
The project is one of the more cost-intensive in comparison
The larger horizontal openings appear too crowded in their proportions
The relationship between building structure and terrain is not convincing in design or programme terms
The high land consumption is not compensated by a clear interior added value
